key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr offered the best combined wear and corrosion performance, while HVOF produced the highest hardness.
engineering_relevance: For WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on 304 stainless steel, HVAF is a promising process choice when both sliding wear and corrosion resistance matter.
method: Deposit WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation spraying, HVOF and HVAF.
Compare microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction, volumetric wear rate and corrosion behavior.
Examine wear marks to identify abrasive and fatigue wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: HVAF achieved a wear rate of (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), versus (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ for uncoated steel, and ranked highest in corrosion resistance with a corrosion current density of (1.75±0.02) μA/cm².
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or corrosion electrolyte, limiting direct transfer of the rankings to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
